questions.question_description: Implement Bubble Sort to sort an array of integers in ascending order. You MUST print the entire array state after each complete pass of the outer loop.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the space-separated array on a new line after each pass. For N>=2, output N-1 lines. For N=0 output an empty line, and for N=1 output a single line with the element.
questions.hints: Compare adjacent elements and swap them if they are in the wrong order. Use an outer loop running N-1 times, and print the array at the end of it.
questions.solution_explanation: Intermediate state printing prevents algorithm evasion.

questions.question_description: Implement Insertion Sort to sort an array of integers in ascending order. You MUST print the entire array state after placing each picked element into its sorted position.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the space-separated array on a new line after each insertion iteration. For N>=2, output N-1 lines. For N=0 output an empty line, and for N=1 output a single line with the element.
questions.hints: Maintain a sorted sub-array at the beginning. Take the next element, 'insert' it, and print the entire array.
questions.solution_explanation: Intermediate state printing prevents algorithm evasion.

questions.question_description: Implement Selection Sort to sort an array of integers in ascending order. You MUST print the entire array state after each minimum-finding and swap pass.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers.
questions.output_format: Print the space-separated array on a new line after each outer loop pass. For N>=2, output N-1 lines. For N=0 output an empty line, and for N=1 output a single line with the element.
questions.hints: Find the minimum element in the unsorted portion, swap it with the first unsorted element, then print the array.
questions.solution_explanation: Intermediate state printing prevents algorithm evasion.
